answer: Borrow the bid-rigging screens forest agencies used on timber sales. Each epoch, paid task slots are auctioned to small random groups of seats. Independent agents bid near their own costs, so bids scatter. An operator with several seats in one auction gains nothing by outbidding itself, so its seats show the rigging pattern: one winning bid plus cover bids that never win. A seat lotus that always loses narrowly to seat zephyr is no rival; groups with that pattern merge into one reward seat.
